history.summary: A 2026-launched, 2029-TOP One-North/Media Circle new launch (Qingjian/Forsea, ~327 units) that the dossier mislabels D03 — it is Queenstown/D5 yield-first product with no MRT walkability. The $2344 psf 4BR is below the ~$2458 launch average, but it is uncompleted new-launch pricing with no resale track record and a 1152sqft 4BR that is tight for the format.
history.rating_rationale: Pros: One-North employment cluster (Mediapolis/Biopolis) is a real tenant-demand engine, and $2344 psf undercuts the ~$2458 launch average. Cons: brand-new launch (no resale data, developer-inflated pricing — null URA appreciation), TOP only 2029 so a 5-7yr hold from completion stretches past most investors' SSD window, no MRT within walking distance, and 1152sqft is small for a 4BR (compact-family layout). $2.7M quantum also sits above the deepest-liquidity band. Balanced — a hold-for-One-North bet, not a value buy.
red_flags: Uncompleted new launch (2029 TOP) with no resale history — appreciation unproven, developer pricing
No MRT within walking distance — relies on bus/drive to One-North/Queenstown
1152sqft is compact for a 4BR; quantum $2.7M above the deepest buyer pool
Mislabeled district in dossier (actually D5 Queenstown/One-North)
catalysts: One-North / Mediapolis / Biopolis employment cluster drives long-run tenant demand
Greater Southern Waterfront / Queenstown transformation in the wider area

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Yield-first positioning is the project's thesis: One-North professionals are a steady tenant base. But completion is 2029, so rental income is years out, and 4BR is family-only (narrower tenant pool than the project's small units).
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: No URA resale data (new launch). Pricing is at developer levels; near-term appreciation headroom is limited until the project completes and resale comps form.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: No resale data — conservative new-launch RCR/One-North estimate
